correctness.rationale: Every dominating set has size at least four since 3 closed cubic neighborhoods cover at most 12 of 14 vertices. Covering inequalities force two point and two line vertices, and the Fano incidence argument yields exactly 21 sets indexed by unordered point pairs. Each vertex lies in 6; same-type pairs lie in 1, nonincident opposite-type pairs in 3, incident pairs in 0. All four traces on nonedges are positive and every triple contains a same-type pair uniquely extending to a concept, so no triple is shattered. The complement graph has 14 vertices and 70 edges and is connected; its integral first cycle rank is 57. A first query positive branch has 6 < 8 concepts, forbidding online depth four, while a fully specified depth-three tree has 8 nonempty leaves. Two independently implemented exhaustive finite checkers in the embedded package reproduce the complete face counts and online dimension.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical cubic Fano incidence geometry and the family of minimum dominating sets is its natural cardinality-optimal covering family. Its Boolean trace complex is unexpectedly the opposite adjacency geometry and has a fully identified 57-cycle integral homotopy type. A precise three-versus-two online/static separation demonstrates an invariant of the minimum-set class not inferable from cardinality or the known 37-maximal-independent-set class; explicit finite proofs make the benchmark reusable without claiming a sweeping extrapolation.
